description:
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the country in which the role is being hired. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

Grants Strategy Manager 

Mark43’s mission is to empower communities and their governments with new technologies that improve the safety and quality of life for all. We build powerful, scalable, and elegant software that sets a new standard for the tools upon which our first responders rely. Our users are diverse, and we are therefore committed to embracing diversity of thought and experience within our team. 

We are looking for a Grants Strategy Manager to join our Business Development & Capture organization. In this role, you will serve as Mark43’s in-house expert on grant funding for state, local, and tribal public safety agencies — helping our customers identify, pursue, and use grant funding to acquire and deploy Mark43 capabilities as authorized expenses. You will work as a customer-facing advisor, plugging into active sales pursuits where grant funding is a meaningful factor, and operating as a strategic partner to the Account Executives and Proposal Managers running those deals. 

This is an individual contributor role for someone who has spent their career at the intersection of public safety operations and grant funding, and who knows how to translate agency needs into compelling, fundable proposals. You will work closely with Mark43’s Account Executives, Proposal Managers, and the Federal Capture Manager, and will report to the VP of Business Development & Capture. Beyond deal support, you will identify funding-led account development opportunities — agencies that are strong grant candidates and represent good inroads for Mark43 — and bring those to Sales as a prospecting motion. Over time, you will help build the operating structure for grants strategy across the broader Mark43 customer base. 

What You’ll Do 

If you were part of our team last week, here are some things you would have done: 

  • Joined a capture call with an Account Executive and a state agency prospect to advise on the federal and state grant programs that could fund their planned RMS, CAD, or analytics modernization — and outlined the timeline and steps the agency would need to take to be ready for the next funding cycle. 
  • Reviewed an upcoming BJA, COPS Office, or DOJ solicitation, identified Mark43 customers and prospects whose needs map to it, and brought a prioritized target list to the relevant Account Executives. 
  • Worked with a customer agency to scope a project narrative that aligns Mark43 capabilities with the funding agency’s priorities and allowable cost categories, and supported the customer’s grant writing efforts where appropriate and permissible. 
  • Advised an agency on the structure of a multi-year project plan that uses grant funding for initial deployment, with clear paths to sustainment funding once the grant period ends. 
  • Identified an agency that is an excellent grant candidate but currently has no active engagement with Mark43, and brought that opportunity to the Account Executive responsible for the territory as a funding-led account development inroad. 
  • Partnered with a Proposal Manager on an active solicitation response, contributing the funding strategy section and ensuring our proposal speaks credibly to the customer’s funding pathway. 
  • Tracked the federal and state grants calendar, surfaced upcoming opportunities to the Sales team, and helped translate funding signals into account-level pursuit actions. 
  • Coordinated the orderly transition of work currently performed by an external grants research vendor into our in-house function, building the playbook, templates, and operating cadence that will support the function long-term. 
  • Educated Account Executives on how to recognize grant-funded opportunities, what questions to ask customers about funding, and when to engage you in a deal. 
  • Worked with the Federal Capture Manager and the Federal Capture Analyst on cross-over opportunities where federal grant programs intersect with state and local pursuits. 

What You’ll Need 

We’re looking for a Grants Strategy Manager with deep, hands-on experience securing and managing grant funding for public safety agencies, and who has worked the customer-facing side of the grants motion in a vendor or consulting capacity. This experience matters because the role requires the judgment to advise customers credibly, the operational fluency to plug into active sales pursuits without slowing them down, and the discipline to operate within the legal and ethical boundaries of a vendor supporting customer grant activities. 

You should also bring: 

  • Significant experience (typically 7+ years) in grant strategy, grant writing, or strategic funding roles supporting public safety, law enforcement, or emergency management agencies. 
  • Demonstrated track record of securing federal and state grant funding, including programs administered by the COPS Office, Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA), Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security, FEMA, and comparable state agencies. 
  • Hands-on familiarity with the federal grants ecosystem — SAM.gov, Grants.gov, agency-specific portals, NOFO and NOFA cycles, allowable cost categories, match requirements, and post-award compliance and reporting. 
  • Strong understanding of state and local grant funding mechanisms, pass-through funding, and the budget cycles of state and local public safety agencies. 
  • Direct operational experience in a public safety or law enforcement agency — enough to credibly advise customers on how grant funding intersects with operational needs, procurement processes, and the realities of implementing technology in active environments. 
  • Experience working with or for technology vendors that serve public safety agencies, including familiarity with how grant strategy supports customer technology procurement decisions. 
  • Strong writing, editing, and communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, compelling, and well-organized funding strategy artifacts and proposal content. 
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple opportunities, deadlines, and customer engagements simultaneously. 
  • Experience partnering with sales, business development, and account management teams in support of customer pursuits. 
  • Practical understanding of the legal and ethical boundaries of vendor support for customer grant activities, and the judgment to operate cleanly within them. 
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred. Certifications such as Certified Grants Management Specialist (CGMS) or Grant Professional Certified (GPC) are a plus. 
  • Passion for supporting public safety, government modernization, and mission-critical technology. 

 

People who thrive on our team also tend to share the following characteristics: 

  • Customer-first and trusted. You build trust quickly with public safety customers and earn the right to advise them on consequential decisions about funding and technology. 
  • Structured and dependable. You bring order to ambiguity, keep teams on track, and create repeatable processes that make grants strategy more effective and scalable over time. 
  • Collaborative and mission-aligned. You enjoy working across teams, value shared success, and care deeply about the public safety mission behind the work. 
  • Strategic and proactive. You look ahead, identify funding opportunities and risks early, and help customers and internal teams make thoughtful decisions on the pursuits where grants are a meaningful factor. 

Where You’ll Work 

Mark43 is a remote-friendly company. For this role, we welcome candidates from across the continental U.S. Occasional travel for customer meetings, conferences, and internal planning sessions is expected. 

Mark43 is approved to hire in Canada, the UK, and 36 U.S. states, including Alabama, Arizona, California (excluding San Francisco), Colorado, Connecticut, Washington D.C., Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Massachusetts, Maryland, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, North Carolina, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia. Before applying to a remote role, please ensure that you are able to perform the position in one of the states listed above. State locations and specifics are subject to change as our hiring requirements shift. 

Our Privacy Notice describes how Mark43 uses and protects the personal information of prospective employees during the recruitment process. It informs you about our handling of the personal information you provide to us when you apply for a position in our organization and in general when you express your interest in joining our team.

As a part of Mark43's security measures all employees must: Engage in appropriate use of the company's electronic information resources; Become knowledgeable about and follow relevant security policies and guidelines; Protect the resources under their control, such as passwords, computers, and data that they create, receive, or download; and Promptly report security-related incidents and violations, and responding to official reports of security incidents involving their systems or accounts.

Mark43 is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please email recruiting@Mark43.com requesting the accommodation.
